rationale: This addEvent is a function declaration local to the domplate IIFE (lines ~14188-15323). The only reference inside that scope is the generated-source string at 14668, which flows via blocks -> fnBlock -> js into a direct eval(js) at 14652 inside the same IIFE, so the eval'd code calls this local addEvent. The bare addEvent(...) calls elsewhere (6943, 8284, 11280, ...) sit inside `with (FBL)` blocks and resolve to FBL.addEvent (this.addEvent at 2560), a different function. dynamic-new-function-dispatch describes exactly this string-to-eval call; eval-based-dynamic-dispatch is limited to dunder-named locals. fp-novel is also defensible because the same-named FBL.addEvent tokens in the file break that rule's literal 'only textual references' precondition.
prior_verdicts_assessment: The eval-based-dynamic-dispatch regression verdict found the right caller but named the dunder-scoped rule rather than dynamic-new-function-dispatch. The two fp-novel verdicts are wrong on the evidence: the bare calls they cite resolve to FBL.addEvent via with(FBL), not this definition.
